acceptance: When a carried patch conflicts or is empty and downstream/staged/<id>.patch exists, refresh candidate/auto applies the staged patch for that entry; if it applies, the refresh continues and integrate writes it as the new normalized patch and removes the staged file.
The drift probe applies the same fallback; a patch whose staged version applies is not drifting, its drift issue closes, and the run summary names it as staged.
A staged patch that also fails is reported as drift with both failures named; a staged file for an unknown or non-carried entry, or one that adds only blank lines, fails the contract test.
Staged files are owned paths in the contract test and are excluded from the current-source reconstruction check.
MAINTAINING.md explains how to stage a resolution and that it is consumed by the next refresh.
After merge, #96 and #97 get staged resolutions (separate PR) and the next scheduled run closes them.
context:
Owner decision 2026-11-17 (choice dialog): staged resolutions chosen over manual refresh at each conflicting tag. Certification counts a release as no-manual when no person acts between the upstream tag and core's merge; staging before the tag is routine maintenance.

Decision gate: none further. If upstream reorders or renames files so a staged patch would touch paths outside its entry's recorded paths, stop and report.

Verification rubric: (1) refresh tests: conflict with a staged fallback refreshes, integrate replaces the patch and deletes the staged file; staged that also fails reports conflict; (2) probe and controller tests: staged fallback closes the drift issue; (3) contract tests for staged files; (4) all downstream suites pass; (5) live: after staging #96/#97, a dry run reports no drift.

Guardrails: the normal patch is always tried first; staged files never change the current source on main; refresh still stops at the first unresolved conflict; no workflow changes (so no human review needed); the controller's write confinement is unchanged.

description: A carried patch must rebuild the current source from the current upstream base (contract test test_normalized_series_reconstructs_current_source), so a patch adapted to new upstream code cannot land before the tag. Drift issues therefore warn but cannot be acted on, and every release that touches patched lines needs a manual refresh (v30.31.0 and v30.33.0 did; drift issues #96 sqlite-date-literals and #97 sqlite-index-null-ordering mean the next tag will too). Add staged resolutions: downstream/staged/<patch-id>.patch, adapted to upstream main, used when the normal patch fails.
